newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU calls for free and fair elections in Zambia.
newsitem.headline: EU calls for free and fair elections in Zambia.

text.p: The European Union said it is closely monitoring Zambia's preparations for elections and it emphasised the need for the highest electoral standards.

"The Union hopes that, even at this late stage, it will still be possible to hold elections which are free and fair and acceptable to all parties, including UNIP," EU President Ireland said in a statement, released late on Thursday, on behalf of the 15-nation bloc.

General elections have been called for November 18 by Zambian president Frederick Chiluba, but former president and main opposition leader Kenneth Kaunda has said his United National Independence Party (UNIP) will boycott the polls.
Controversial constitutional changes passed in May by a parliament dominated by Chiluba supporters prevent Kaunda from running for president, but UNIP is free to take part.

Kaunda, president for almost three decades until Chiluba ousted him in Zambia's first free elections in 1991, has dismissed the elections as a sham, saying Chuiluba had changed the rules and tampered with the voters' register.
